_comment: Evidence Source Registry. Every legitimate source the system may use or acquire from, with licence and access facts. Adding a source = an entry here (and, for a new access method, a connector class registered in backend/app/knowledge_engine/acquisition.py). Institutions, datasets and companies appear only here, never in analytics code. Runtime state (last_success / last_failure / attempts) lives in source_registry_state.json and is written only by scripts/acquisition/acquire_evidence.py.

sources.license: supplied by the project owner (exports of public job boards); used for analysis only, not redistributed
sources.provenance_policy: sha256 verified against the manifest before ingestion

sources.license: declared per file in <file>.source.json (files without a declared licence are quarantined)
sources.provenance_policy: sidecar <file>.source.json with source_url, licence, collected_on, geographic_scope, collected_by

sources.license: Jooble REST API terms: requires a personal API key and acceptance of Jooble's terms; redistribution of results is not granted
sources.provenance_policy: raw JSON response stored with request time and query
sources.note: disabled until the owner obtains a key and accepts the terms; no client is shipped (it cannot be validated without a key)

sources.license: official PDFs published by the institutions / AICTE (see manifest source_url)

sources.provenance_policy: sidecar <file>.source.json with official source_url, institution, programme, version, role

sources.license: official institution website; download by a person, keep the source URL
sources.provenance_policy: only official institution PDFs; placed in the curricula drop folder with a sidecar

sources.license: ESCO: European Commission, free re-use with attribution (Commission Decision 2011/833/EU)
ESCO: European Commission, free re-use with attribution

sources.temporal_scope: O*NET release placed by the owner
sources.license: O*NET: CC BY 4.0 (U.S. Department of Labor/ETA)
sources.provenance_policy: sidecar with release version and download URL; a US taxonomy is kept as a separate scope, never mixed into the India population

requirements.analysis: industry trends / emerging and declining skills
requirements.why_it_matters: a trend needs the same population observed in at least two periods; with one period every trend is INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
a peer comparison needs at least one curriculum of a peer institution; a model/regulatory REFERENCE curriculum is not a peer
occupation-group demand comparisons need most postings mapped to an occupation

requirements.analysis: semantic accuracy / promotion gate on independent labels
requirements.why_it_matters: model precision can only be claimed against labels made by an independent person; without them the model stays in SAFE_MODE
